quest.title: Long Live Life
quest.description: Strange ink blots wander around the Luyang Academy...

chapter.num: A Long Day in the Mountains: Chapter 1
chapter.title: Paradise

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry to keep you waiting. Looks like things went smoothly for you guys, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Daozi, can you believe it? We ran into a fake Escher!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You fill Daozi in about what just happened...

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Hmph. This must be Melanta working from behind the curtain.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: To him, names are nothing but a string of numbers slapped onto us when we arrive here.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: How would he know that "Maukie" was a nickname that Escher's grandfather and father gave him in his childhood?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But as it turned out, everyone here gets along so well that you all call him that now.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Just because we were somewhat... unsettled by his paintings doesn't mean we dislike him.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: It's just that messing with space is a grave issue around here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That only makes Paimon want to see his work even more.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: You'll get the chance to see it, I'm sure.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Now that we've got the whole set of paintings, one stroke is all we need to connect them. Allow my clumsy hand to provide that finishing touch.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: After all, I did coach Kanou on his Liyue landscape paintings. He won't mind me adding a little something.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Through this painting, you should be able to reach the Pavilion of Paintings at the center.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Once you're inside, try reaching out and plucking the heavenly heart.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: It just occurred to me — "adding feet to a dragon" and "dotting the eyes of a dragon" are both sayings concerning dragons.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: But their meanings are worlds apart.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They sure are.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Reach out your hand and touch the painting. Break this veil of illusion, and the world beyond shall receive you once more.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: In simpler terms, touch the painting, and you'll be able to return. Though the world outside is just another illusion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It won't open. {NICKNAME}, how about giving it a real nasty kick?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Kick forcefully)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How is it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I can't feel my leg.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pfff...

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Touching this screen should do it.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Then, try to pluck the star.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: These photos...

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Ah, they were painted using a Kamera, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Back then, your sister told us of something capable of creating pictures even more lifelike than the most realistic paintings.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: We all wondered what it would be like.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: It's a shame that she didn't have a Kamera, nor did she have a picture painted by it on hand.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Now that I've seen one myself, it does look incredibly lifelike.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, how's that for feeling smug? Machines have taken realism to its natural end, but there's still room for imagination, y'know?

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Not exactly. No matter how realistic the painting, it still carries the painter's emotions and aesthetic sense.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Though some of the colors can't be found in the real world, you can really feel the painter's heart from the way said colors are used.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Even the most realistic painting carries within it minor details of fiction, exaggeration, and blur. That's where the artist's aesthetics and craft come into play.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... It's not like Paimon doesn't get it. Paimon just wanted to compliment you so she could ask you to, y'know, maybe draw something for us later...?

choices.text: Don't you already have Albedo's painting of you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wants to see what a more expressive version of her would look like, though!

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Thank you so much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Zeitlind, could Paimon have a look?

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Sure. These photos were taken during my sister's vacation.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: The passerby she asked was really bad at photography, so some photos only show the top of her head poking out from the bottom.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: But I can tell that she's smiling happily all the same.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: Sorry to let you see that. The lighting and composition of these photos are terrible. There's no sense of depth or layering at all.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: It's not that bad. I think these are the best... uh, pho-toes.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: If your sister hadn't insisted on only showing her head, these would've been the worst of scenic paintings... I mean, scenic photos.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: But thanks to her, they have become memories and proof of her presence there.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: ...I think I get what you mean.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: I've found my stuff. Let's keep helping Daozi out, shall we?

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: I think the painting there leads to the Abode of Resplendent Talent. See if you can find a way to the Tower of Radiant Light from there.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: That said, I won't be joining you for your next journey.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: I'll head back to the central area to let others know we're safe. Then I'll be back in no time.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: Whether I succeed or not, I should have enough time to see you again on my way back.

choices.text: Could we take it with us?

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: I don't think you could take it with you. Otherwise, you'd make a lot of Mora from selling my paintings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lots of Mora, huh? Were you a famous painter or something?

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: "Let me have a look. Hmm, I can't believe I'm looking at an authentic Yunlai Daoxuan! And painted just last week, too!"

talks.objective: Use Dex's ability to restore the space in the painting

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Looks like everything's going smoothly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Istoria! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Daozi told me that you had arrived at Luyang Academy, so I came along with him.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: How's the search going? Have you found what you were looking for this time, Zeitlind?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I have.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Could you tell me what it was that landed in Luyang Academy this time? This is the place of painters, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: And to tell the truth, I haven't a foggiest what it might be.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Photos from my sister's Kamera.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: A Kamera... I've heard people talking about such devices before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, you're falling behind. The painters have all heard about Kameras from Zeitlind's sister.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: That's because people here focus on the visual arts. It's normal that she'd talk to them about it.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The thing I discussed most with Hilda was... philosophy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Philosophy!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: It's hard to imagine my sister talking about this with someone as knowledgeable as you.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Oh, you flatter me. We weren't getting into any deep or complex debates. We were just chatting about how to look at the everyday things around us.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: For example, the most fundamental question of philosophy is whether one should or shouldn't end it all tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Allow me to explain. In a sense, our inquiry into the world is a search for the very meaning of our existence within it.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Whether we are the children seated upon the gods' knees, or merely echoes in the winds of inconstant time...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: All of that is too far removed. How can an ordinary person weigh themselves against the universe? For most, the "world" is no more than their own life.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: If we one day discover that everything is destined to return to nothingness in the far future, would our lives now still hold meaning?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Or, should our lives be a shoreless sea of suffering to begin with, then the world may in truth be but a collection of agonies.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: In either case, there is no difference between living and not. In the latter, death might even be called a release.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon... Paimon doesn't think that's right. Not that she knows how to argue against you, though.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: And what was my sister's response?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Never mind that. I was the one arguing that even if life is inherently meaningless, we should still choose to live it.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Ah, it seems you haven't heard.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I saw my sister's tombstone back at the sanatorium.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Thanks for trying to save her in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: What's written on her epitaph?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: "One lifetime doesn't count."

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Is that what it says?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zeitlind...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I can hardly believe it myself, and I wish I could say something to take your pain away.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Give me some time, though.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: You don't have to say anything.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I thought I'd cry the moment I saw her tombstone, but as it turned out, I was unusually calm.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: It would have been better if I had cried.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: That's not what I meant.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Anyway... you'll understand later.

dialogues.speaker: "Maukie"
dialogues.text: Hello, my name is Escher. I'm a painter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you're the "Maukie" that Istoria was talking about? The one who did all those amazing paintings?

dialogues.speaker: "Maukie"
dialogues.text: Yeah. My birth name was Escher, though.

dialogues.speaker: "Maukie"
dialogues.text: Anyway, please come with me, I'll take you somewhere safe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we're not looking for a safe place. We're here to solve the problem.

dialogues.speaker: "Maukie"
dialogues.text: If that's the case, you should also come with me. I'll take you where you need to go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These melons...

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are they ripe?

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon means, are you sure they're ready to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: That doesn't matter.

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: Zeitlind, the two of us used to teach your sister how to draw.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: That's her signature...

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: And since it's her stuff, you should be the one to keep them and take them away from this place.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: What do you think of this painting?

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: How should I put it? Some people can paint on par with masters in their teenage years, and so they spent the rest of their lives searching for paintings imbued with childlike innocence.

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: I can neither discern a masterful temper nor childlike innocence from Hilda's painting.

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: Instead, it is tinged with sadness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't the sadness conveyed by painting the fruit impressive enough?

dialogues.speaker: Raumhilda
dialogues.text: Really? Are you telling me this painting is devoid of childlike charm and doesn't look like a master's work?

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Talent and diligent practice are prerequisites for cultivating the spirit of a master.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: So, uh, why don't you forget what we've taught and do another painting?

dialogues.speaker: Raumhilda
dialogues.text: You guys are hilarious.

dialogues.speaker: Raumhilda
dialogues.text: I'm not doing another painting. I've experienced it once already, and I find it quite interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Raumhilda
dialogues.text: But just as a canvas, once colored, cannot return to pristine white, how could I possibly forget what I've learned?

dialogues.speaker: Raumhilda
dialogues.text: Let the mediocre piece be as it is.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Is that so? So it's just a mediocre piece.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: And yet... she still signed her name on it.

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: Yes. When we artists take commissions, we always use secret signatures to sign our work.

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: So she named the painting "Long Live Life"... and then she left.

dialogues.speaker: Yoshitoshi
dialogues.text: What do you think? Are you going to take her painting with you?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: No, let it stay where it belongs.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Such paintings may become lost and destroyed in less than a hundred years if brought outside. Better let it repose in eternal peace here with you.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: I see.

talks.objective: Use Dex's ability to restore the space in the painting

dialogues.speaker: Yoshitoshi
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, I haven't seen Maukie anywhere. Did he end up trapped in the Desert Pavilion?

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: That's on you lot. Why did you lure him into the construction site anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Yoshitoshi
dialogues.text: We weren't excluding him or anything! We just wanted him to show the people from the "Desert Pavilion" how shocking the spatial distortion is. After all, they're the ones who are so obsessed with space.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Messing with space might break the rules around here. He's probably been "forcibly exiled" by Melanta by now.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Mountains cannot crush the buried spirit; through riven clouds, the sky at last appears. I'm free!

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Hilda, Dex, and my new friends, please, accept my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I'm her younger sister, Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Oh? Why, you two look so alike!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Yes, I've been told that a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: And who are these two?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #My name's Paimon! And this is {NICKNAME}. It was Istoria's commission that brought us here.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: In that case, let's dispense with the introductions. Do you possess any degree of martial skill? Preferably of the sort that might see off a Legatus of Remuria.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just how did you come up with that description?

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Ah, this goes back to how a certain border fortress rose to prominence when Remuria was destroyed.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: One day, after much time had passed, an old man arrived at its gates, claiming to be the acting master of the Guhua Clan.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: One day, the two sides fell to arguing.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: When the Remurian commander said that he was in charge of music in the army, the acting master thought him weak.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: But in truth, the greater your musical mastery, the higher your rank in the Remurian military. And this commander, why, he had already undergone petrification!

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: By the way, I don't know if you've heard of this, but everyone in the Remurian inner circles was transformed into "Ichor," becoming semi-immortal golems.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: So, when the acting master channeled his inner energies into a single strike, he only wound up hurting his own hand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhhh...

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: He then spoke harshly, lamenting a lack of successors to the Guhua Clan's secret arts and the withering of talent on the vine in his era. Why, so he claimed, he didn't even possess a Vision!

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: — Of course, he wouldn't have been selected if he had one in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: After enduring the Apathic Interval, we could no longer receive Visions... But anyway, back to our story.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: The commander shot back with choice words of his own, claiming that the Legati of Remuria were far more terrifying than he could ever be.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Eh, sure. Cool story, Paimon supposes? Also, don't worry. {NICKNAME}'s one thousand percent got what it takes to defeat a Legatus.

choices.text: With both hands tied behind my back, even!

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: Hahaha, that's great.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: By the way, why were you in the painting? And what are those humanoid ink blots?

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: This is how Melanta delivers punishment: Sealing people into paintings and smushing them into ink blots.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: Just like my cage, which was encased in layers of paintings.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So the ink blots we saw back there were actually... people?

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: Now, a word to the wise.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: The more realistic a painting is, the more fitting a cage it is to ensconce your spirit. After all, its essence may be grasped at a glance.

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: As such, expect hidden secrets lurking behind any realistic paintings you find here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And what should we do next?

response.speaker: Daozi
response.text: This is not the right place for such talk. Let's head back first.

choices.text: Best that I keep a low profile, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. We sure made it back quickly!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: This place truly is full of wonders.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: It is indeed fabulous, comparable to the finishing touch from Rex Lapis's hand, which brought stone to life.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: And with the power of your heart and mind, you can really turn those lifelike paintings into reality.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, what's our next plan of action?

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: The key to restoring the entire library lies in completing that final, illuminating stroke. But before we do that, we must first restore this painting.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: "Once the Heavenly Heart Emerges, the Four Horizons Fade to White."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What a commanding name.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: That's Inazuman preferences in painting names for you.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Theoretically, we should be able to complete the missing part of the painting in the Tower of Radiant Light.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: But with our path barred, it seems we can only head to the Abode of Resplendent Talent to see if we can reach the Tower of Radiant Light from there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, it was behind this door the whole time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon had {NICKNAME} kick this thing, full force! {NICKNAME}'s strong enough to level mountains, but the door didn't even budge.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Is your foot numb?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah...

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Probably because this door was manifested from the painting through the mind. As such, it doesn't exist as physical matter as we know it.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Istoria once mentioned that he had a teacher named Aristocles, who was always saying that "mind prevails over matter." I guess this is what they meant.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: But leveling mountains, you say... That would make you just as powerful as Azhdaha. Speaking of which...

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Yu Huangyi from the Mahavaipulya Chamber told me that Azhdaha already existed back in his era.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: As such, the so-called "finishing touch" that brought the dragon to life was nothing more than a legend, the invention of later generations. A fine story all the same, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And did you realize something from that?

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: I just told him, "You've ruined a precious memory, you know that?"

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I can relate.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: *sigh* Never mind, just take it as a fun little anecdote. Anyway, since the door was born from a painting, a painter must open it. Allow me to do that for you.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: You don't seem very surprised.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That's because {NICKNAME}'s been through even crazier stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Lots of extraordinary adventures, huh? Guess I shouldn't even be surprised if you've saved the world before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{F#She}{M#He} and {F#her brother}{M#his sister} were separated by an awful god.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #The main goal of our adventure is to find {F#her}{M#his} lost sibling.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #So {NICKNAME} can understand how you feel.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I hope you find your sibling, and may you live a life of peace and happiness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Paimon's sorry. She forgot that you won't...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Ah, please, don't apologize. It was my fault for bringing it up. Also, that's not what I meant.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I really hope that your wish comes true.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you, Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Alright. Open sesame!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's get moving, then!

talks.objective: Head to the Abode of Resplendent Talent
Use Dex's ability to restore the space in the painting

dialogues.speaker: "Maukie"
dialogues.text: Hello, my name is Escher. I'm a painter.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you're the "Maukie" that Istoria was talking about? The one who did all those amazing paintings?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, Paimon just remembered... Have we met before?

dialogues.speaker: "Maukie"
dialogues.text: No, and Escher was my birth name, so...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, really? Do you have any brothers who suddenly disappeared?

dialogues.speaker: "Maukie"
dialogues.text: I'm afraid not.

dialogues.speaker: "Maukie"
dialogues.text: Anyway, please come with me, I'll take you somewhere safe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we're not looking for a safe place. We're here to solve the problem.

dialogues.speaker: "Maukie"
dialogues.text: If that's the case, you should also come with me. I'll take you where you need to go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. Weird guy. Eh, whatever. Let's follow him and see what he's up to.

talks.objective: Don't let the ink blot catch you!

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: Kanou, Yoshitoshi, Bosch, you've all come back to life!

dialogues.speaker: Kanou
dialogues.text: Ah, yeah. And I never want to paint another screen again.

dialogues.speaker: Daozi
dialogues.text: #Good to have you back, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and our young Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Yoshitoshi
dialogues.text: I owe you all a great deal.

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: You really look like Hilda.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: She's my older sister.

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: I know, I know... This old man's still got an eye for people.

dialogues.speaker: Bosch
dialogues.text: Speaking of which... Zeitlind, come here for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It won't open. {NICKNAME}, how about giving it a hard kick?
